stories.story: As a buyer or agent, I can create an account, sign in and out, and recover access so my data persists across devices.
ac: Given a new email, when I register and enter the emailed code within 15 minutes, then my account is created and I am signed in.
Given I forgot my password or lost my device, when I request recovery, then I receive a single-use link that expires in 30 minutes and does not reveal whether the email exists.
Given 5 failed sign-ins in 15 minutes, then further attempts are throttled and the event is logged.
Given I saved homes on this device before signing in, when I sign in, then they merge into my account without duplicates.
stories.done: Prototype stand-in only: a "Viewing as" role switcher (ADR 0011). Guests are asked to sign in before saving, sharing or planning inspections. No real accounts, recovery or throttling yet.

stories.story: As the platform, I enforce role-based permissions for buyer, agent, agency admin, moderator and platform admin.
ac: Every API route declares the roles allowed; a route without a declaration fails CI.
A buyer token calling any agent or admin endpoint receives 403 and the attempt is logged.
An agent can only act on listings belonging to their verified agency.
Role changes are made only by a platform admin, require a reason and are audit-logged (FR-ADM-002).
stories.done: Prototype: role table in apps/web/lib/roles.ts enforced on pages and server actions; agent scope checks; refused actions logged; role change needs platform admin and reason. Tests in lib/roles.test.ts.

epics.title: Search
epics.workstream: WS2 Consumer PWA / WS6 AI Concierge

stories.story: As a buyer, I can search pilot listings with natural language or structured filters.
ac: Given any combination of suburb, type, price, bedrooms, bathrooms, parking, land size, features and open-home day, results satisfy every mandatory constraint (verified by property-based tests).
Results are paginated, sortable by relevance, price and newest, and the URL captures the full query so it can be shared and reloaded.
p95 search response under the target set in NFR-PERF-001 at the pilot load in docs/data/pilot-sizing.md.
stories.done: Prototype: rule-based NL parser and filters on synthetic data.

stories.story: As a buyer, I see how my words were interpreted as editable criteria before I trust the results.
ac: Every criterion applied appears as a chip and in the editable Criteria panel.
Every assumption (e.g. '3 bed' read as 'at least 3') is listed in plain words.
Requests the platform cannot judge (investment quality, school quality, safety) are named as unsupported and never converted into hidden filters.
Editing any criterion re-runs the search without re-interpreting the original text.

stories.story: As a buyer, I get honest help when there are zero results, ambiguity, missing data or a service failure.
ac: Zero results shows a clear empty state with up to 3 single-change refinements, each showing how many homes it would return.
Ambiguous input (e.g. 'under 900') asks one clarifying question and shows the assumption used meanwhile.
Listings with hidden prices are excluded from price-filtered results and the count excluded is stated.
If the AI provider fails or times out (threshold in ADR 0006), search falls back to structured filters with a visible notice and a concierge_failure event.
stories.done: Prototype covers zero results, ambiguity and hidden prices; AI fallback not yet applicable.

stories.story: As a buyer, I see current listing data, media, agent/agency, inspections and status from the canonical model.
ac: Every field shown maps to a canonical schema field and shows its source and last-updated time.
Withdrawn, sold or unpublished listings return a clear 'no longer available' page (HTTP 404/410), never stale data.
Listing pages are server-rendered with canonical URL, metadata and structured data (NFR-SEO-001).

stories.story: As a buyer, I see licensed enrichment (sales history, estimates, suburb stats) with attribution.
ac: Enrichment is visually separated from agent-supplied data and names its provider and effective date.
Until a data licence exists, placeholder figures carry a 'Placeholder, not an estimate' label and cannot be shown in production (feature flag).
Enrichment never overwrites current listing fields; conflicts are flagged (V11 §12.7).

stories.story: As a buyer, I see the listing's compliance-readiness status.
ac: The disclosure panel lists each rule outcome from the active pack with its version.
Wording confirms readiness of documents, never their content, and states it is not legal advice.

stories.story: As a signed-in buyer, I can save listings and organise them into collections.
ac: Save/unsave is one tap from results and detail, optimistic, and rolls back with a message on failure.
I can create, rename and delete collections and move listings between them.
A saved listing that is withdrawn stays in the collection marked 'no longer available'.

stories.story: As a buyer, I can share a stable link and invite collaborators to a collection.
ac: Sharing a listing uses the native share sheet, falling back to copy-link.
Collection invites grant view or edit access, can be revoked, and expire after 14 days if unaccepted.
A revoked or unauthorised user opening a collection link sees an access message, not the contents.

stories.story: As a buyer, I can add published open-home times to my inspection timeline.
ac: Only inspection windows from the listing feed can be added; changes in the feed update the timeline and notify me.
Listings with no upcoming opens show an 'arrange a private inspection' prompt.

stories.story: As a buyer, I get a feasible sequence with travel buffers and clear conflict warnings.
ac: Given saved listings with valid windows, the plan orders visits to fit the most homes with the least driving, including parking and visit time.
Homes that cannot fit are listed separately with the reason (window closes before arrival, overlap).
Drive times state how they were estimated.

stories.story: As a buyer, I can reorder visits and record notes and ratings after each inspection.
ac: Manual reordering recalculates times and conflicts immediately; I can return to the suggested order.
Notes (up to 2,000 characters) and a 1–5 rating save per listing and are private to me unless shared.

stories.story: As a buyer, concierge answers use approved sources and cite material facts.
ac: Every material factual claim in an answer links to a canonical field, rule result or approved document.
Benchmark citation correctness meets the threshold approved by PO and AI Lead (docs/ai/benchmark.md).

stories.story: As a buyer, the concierge never invents attributes, prices, zoning, eligibility or guaranteed outcomes.
ac: When data is missing the answer says so and offers to ask the agent.
Adversarial benchmark cases (docs/ai/benchmark-cases.json, category 'adversarial') pass at 100%.
Answers never contain personalised financial advice, return predictions or legal conclusions.

stories.story: As the platform, AI calls go through a router with model routing, limits, caching and cost circuit-breakers.
ac: Model, prompt version and cost are logged per call.
Per-user and global daily spend limits are configurable; when hit, the concierge degrades to structured search.
Swapping the primary model is a configuration change validated by re-running the benchmark.

stories.story: With consent, the concierge remembers approved preferences across sessions.
ac: Memory is off until I opt in, and I can view and delete what is remembered.
Remembered items are limited to the approved list in the data inventory.

stories.story: As a first home buyer, eligibility is decided by deterministic rules before any AI explanation.
ac: Results come only from the active versioned rule pack; the LLM may rephrase but not change an outcome.
Unknown answers produce 'need more information', never a guess.
Answers are not stored unless I opt in to saving them (V11 §12.5).

stories.story: As a first home buyer, each result shows its source, version, effective date and assumptions.
ac: Each scheme result names the official source and the date it was checked.
The rules version, status (draft/active) and effective date appear with the results.

stories.story: As the platform, listing rights require licence verification or an approved exception.
ac: An unverified agent cannot publish; the Publish control is disabled with the reason.
An exception requires a platform admin, a reason and an expiry date, and is audit-logged.
A licence that lapses unpublishes affected listings within 24 hours.
stories.done: Rule QLD-AGT-001 in pack. Prototype: Publish disabled with reason; platform admin approves an exception with reason and expiry (audit-logged).

stories.story: As an agent, my console shows onboarding, feed status, listings, exceptions and publication status.
ac: Feed status shows last run, records received/rejected and the reason per rejection.
Exceptions are grouped blocking, incomplete and warning, each with a fix action.
stories.done: Prototype /agent: licence status, feed runs with rejection reasons, listings grouped by gate result with the rule pack's fix text.

stories.story: As an authorised agent, I can preview, resolve exceptions, publish, unpublish and update supported states.
ac: Preview renders exactly the buyer view.
Corrected data re-runs the publication gate and publishes automatically when all mandatory checks pass.
Unpublish takes effect in search within 60 seconds.
stories.done: Prototype: buyer-view preview, publish/unpublish (gate re-checked on the server; unpublish removes it from search). Auto-republish on corrected data not built.

stories.story: As an agent, I can answer listing Q&A and receive buyer details only after consent.
ac: Buyer identity is hidden in Q&A unless the buyer chose to share it.
A lead appears only with a recorded consent (who, what, when, purpose).

stories.story: As the platform, I ingest REAXML and map it to the canonical model.
ac: All fields in docs/data/reaxml-mapping.md map with tests; unmapped elements are logged, not dropped silently.
Times are converted with the listing's state time zone.
stories.done: Adapter with 12 tests on sample feeds.

stories.story: As an operator, ingestion validates, updates idempotently, logs errors and can reprocess.
ac: Replaying the same (agency, uniqueID, modTime) changes nothing.
Invalid records are rejected with a line-level reason and do not block valid records in the same file.
An admin can reprocess a failed file; the result is audit-logged.
stories.done: Adapter idempotency and rejection reasons tested.

stories.story: As the platform, a configurable jurisdiction rules engine evaluates mandatory publication requirements.
ac: Rules live in versioned JSON packs, not code; a new pack version needs no deployment.
Missing facts evaluate to unknown, never pass.

stories.story: As the platform, I block publication when mandatory rules fail and give an actionable reason.
ac: A listing failing any blocking rule is never visible to buyers.
Each failure names the rule, what is missing and how to fix it.

stories.story: As a compliance owner, rule-pack changes are versioned, audited and regression-tested.
ac: Every pack has fixtures; CI fails if any fixture outcome changes without a version bump.
Activating a pack requires a second approver and records who, when and why.
stories.done: Fixtures + tests; activation workflow not built.

stories.story: As a platform admin, I manage users, agents, agencies, listings, verification exceptions, feed failures and moderation.
ac: Each queue shows count, oldest item age and SLA breach.
Admin access requires MFA (NFR-SEC-003).
stories.done: Prototype /admin: queues with counts, users and roles, agencies, verification exceptions, feed failures, moderation queue (empty: Q&A is P1). No MFA or SLA targets yet.

stories.story: As an auditor, privileged actions affecting publication, compliance, identity or moderation are auditable.
ac: Audit records are append-only with actor, action, target, before/after, reason and time.
Audit records are retained for 7 years (to confirm in PIA) and exportable.
stories.done: audit_log table in migration 0001. Prototype: read-only in-memory audit log of publish, role and verification actions and refused attempts. No export or retention yet.

stories.story: As the PO, I can see weekly active buyers per pilot suburb and inspection-timeline depth from day one.
ac: All 33 §12.8 events validate against the catalogue; invalid events are rejected and counted.
Both launch KPIs compute from SQL views with no manual steps.

stories.story: As a buyer, I can ask listing-specific questions, subject to moderation.
ac: Questions are moderated before public display; the agent's answer is labelled as from the agent.
Reported content is hidden pending review.

stories.story: As a buyer, I have a profile and can follow properties and suburbs and get notifications.
ac: Following a property notifies me of price, status and inspection changes.
Notification preferences are per channel and default to off for marketing.

stories.story: As a buyer, Suburb Hub v1 shows approved seeded content without open commenting.
ac: Content carries author and provenance; no user comments in v1.

stories.story: As a buyer, Trending v1 is derived from defined events and excludes invalid or abusive activity.
ac: Trending uses listing_viewed/saved/shared with per-user caps and bot filtering.

stories.story: As the platform, intent signals may be computed internally but buyer details go to agents only with consent.
ac: No intent threshold triggers disclosure; lead_sent requires a prior lead_consent_granted.

stories.story: As a buyer, I can pin approved listing images and features to boards with attribution.
ac: Pins keep listing attribution and disappear if the listing media is withdrawn.
